claim: Sourced Be-free faces do not float; the 60% Vf projection needs CHECK-049's consistent mixture and reoptimization.
source_report_body:
QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. MAINLINE-049 complete, folding in 048's finish and water, CHECK-040's rows and simjob.

No beryllium-free P2 floats on sourced faces at R 15-30, either weather, even at all four optimism endpoints. Under 048's account the closest, quasi-isotropic K13D2U on 5056 bonded at room temperature, is short 1.0/1.9/4.8 t and needs 7-12% more modulus. AlBeMet: short 1.7-10.0 t, and 62% beryllium. M55J: short 2.9-19.5 t. Aramid cores are crimp-bound, and undried their water breaks the service pressure. CFRP bonded to 5056 at 200 F fails the free edge (0.55); it needs a bond at or below 50 C.

One projection floats: K13D2U at 60% Vf (200 GPa), on gamma, Q and face compression. R 30 ISA usage 0.721 (gamma x1.95, Q x1.93, 293 MPa). Endpoints +1.6/+4.3/+16.3 t. Beryllium floats on gamma and Q alone (usage 0.72/0.60/0.53).

CHECK-040's rows: at 1 mm of water only R 30 floats. Cure in the global and crimp demand costs the floating builds at most 0.45 t; edge/scarf costs beryllium 0.2-1.4 t and the CFRP nothing. No float is lost. The 60% Vf face fails 048's full-cycle screen at 037's geometry (0.890) and passes at its own (1.18).

Supply at R 30: 4.8% of pitch-fibre capacity, against 24% of world beryllium.

Easier to ground: beryllium's optimisms, fewer and smaller, on a sourced face. The CFRP's case is supply.

Checks: 040's 12 rows; 048's 8 bit for bit; CHECK-040's 28 within 0.0006 kg. Results come from simjob runs; two earlier bare runs repeated identically. 17 NFI.
